findings.repair: Leave the code as it stands. The omission is deliberate, reasoned, and mechanically pinned: `tests/guides.test.ts:67-73` names all five in the parity `INTERNAL` list with the reason in its doc block, `tests/guides.test.ts:121-128` asserts in both directions that a name on that list is stranded and that nothing stranded is missing from it — so the list cannot rot in either direction — and `guides/codec.md:61-64` and `:106-107` state the same ruling to the reader ("the alphabets and the reverse lookups behind them are module data, not public API, because publishing an alphabet invites hand-rolling the coding it belongs to"). If the Orchestrator instead rules that the fleet's `INTERNAL` mechanism covers classes alone, the alternative repair is to add `export * from './constants.js'` to `src/core/index.ts`, delete the five rows from `INTERNAL`, and add a Surface row plus a worked `@example` for each constant to `guides/codec.md`; that is additive to the published surface and breaks nothing, but it publishes the alphabets the charter exists to keep unpublished.

referrals: To the subjective lane (S6 Guide and README parity): `guides/README.md:17-30` carries a `## Dependency reference` section explaining why the vendored `guide.md` and `scaffold.md` mirrors sit in the guides directory, but `guides/test.md` and `guides/probe.md` sit beside them unnamed anywhere in the index. I refuse this as an objective finding — `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Authority and workflow requires a concept index and a directory index, and both are complete and correct — and no sibling fleet package names `test.md` or `probe.md` in its index either, so it is a fleet-wide voice question rather than a codec defect. Whether the section that undertakes to explain the mirrors may name only some of them is the subjective lane's call.

To the subjective lane (S1 Entity API shape / S4 Design laws): each `is*` guard answers by allocating. `isBase64` (validators.ts:28) calls `decodeBase64`, which allocates the full decoded byte array to answer a boolean, while `measureBase64` (helpers.ts:230) walks the identical grammar and allocates nothing. The same holds for `isBase64URL` and `isHex`. The design is deliberate and documented — `guides/codec.md:51-55` states that the guard answers by asking its partial function so the two sets cannot drift, and that a measure exists precisely because it never allocates — so I raise no objective finding. Whether the package's own stated reason for the measures argues that the guards ought to ask them instead is a coherence question for the subjective lane.

To the Orchestrator (canon versus instrument, scaffold-owned files): `.claude/rules/architecture.md` § What the policy sweep proves enumerates what the sweep covers and closes the list with 'no later version of the sweep claims more', but the vendored `tests/setupPolicy.ts` also enforces a test-to-module mirror rule (`inspectPolicyMirrors`, setupPolicy.ts:880, wired in at :1946, with its own control rows at :2097-2134) that the rules file does not list. Both files are off-limits as subjects for this round, and the gap cost me a full verification pass to establish which side of finding codec-obj-1 the sweep actually stands on. Neither file is a codec defect; the canon and the instrument belong in the same hand.
